title: Subqueries with IN
description: A subquery can also produce a whole list of values to test membership against with IN, instead of a single number. Write a query that returns the `first_name` and `last_name` of every customer who has placed at least one order (without using a JOIN).
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: subquery with IN

(SELECT customer_id FROM orders) produces a list of every customer_id that has ordered - IN checks whether a column's value appears anywhere in that list, the same way it would against a hand-typed list of numbers.
SELECT first_name, last_name FROM customers WHERE id IN (a subquery selecting customer_id FROM orders).
expected_behavior: Returns first_name and last_name for customers whose id appears among orders.customer_id.
solution: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders);
explanation: IN with a subquery is often interchangeable with a JOIN for this kind of "does a match exist" question, but it keeps the output shaped like the outer table alone - one row per customer, not one row per matching order.
